subject: Apply a function column wise on a whole data.frame

messages.author: fc22cb727156ff4f
messages.subject: Apply a function column wise on a whole data.frame
parts:
Hi everyone,

I want to apply a function to each column of a data.frame and get a
data.frame as result. If I was doing this on different subsets of the
data.frame, I would do:

data <- data.frame(a=runif(10), b=rnorm(10), c=rep(c(1,2), each=5))
library("plyr")
ddply(data, ~c, colwise(function(x){mean(x)+sd(x)}))

but here I want to use *all* lines of the data.frame. So I ended up doing:

data <- data[,-3]
colwise(function(x){mean(x)+sd(x)})(data)

but it "feels" wrong. Is there a more natural way (even in plain R,
not necessarily plyr)? It looks like I want sapply but which returns a
data.frame. as.data.frame(sapply(...)) transposes the data.frame, just
as ldply does and I don't want that.

Thanks in advance. Sincerely,

JiHO

messages.subject: Re: Apply a function column wise on a whole data.frame
parts:
> but here I want to use *all* lines of the data.frame. So I ended up doing:
>
> data <- data[,-3]
> colwise(function(x){mean(x)+sd(x)})(data)
>
> but it "feels" wrong. Is there a more natural way (even in plain R,
> not necessarily plyr)? It looks like I want sapply but which returns a
> data.frame. as.data.frame(sapply(...)) transposes the data.frame, just
> as ldply does and I don't want that.

That's exactly what colwise was designed to do.

In base R, you could do data.frame(lapply(data, function(x) mean(x)+sd(x) ))

Hadley

messages.author: fc22cb727156ff4f
messages.subject: Re: Apply a function column wise on a whole data.frame
parts:
Thanks for the replies. Either:

data.frame(apply(data, 2, function(x) mean(x) + sd(x)))

or

data.frame(lapply(data, function(x) mean(x)+sd(x) ))

work indeed. I was focused on sapply after reading the source of
colwise() and Filter() but I should have though of those.
> That's exactly what colwise was designed to do.

I was thinking that there was a **ply construct that I was missing. I
will use colwise then.

Thanks again.

JiHO
